summary: Beam shape, feed lines, waveguide, the slotted array, and how the antenna's bearing reaches the display.

blocks.title: The beam
items: Bearing resolution largely depends on a narrow antenna beam in the horizontal plane. A wide beam merges 2 close ships.
Vertical beam: fairly wide, so targets stay in view as the ship rolls.
Longer antenna, narrower horizontal beam. Off to the side, waves from the 2 ends fall out of step and cancel.
X-band: about 9.4 GHz, a wavelength of about 3.2 cm, roughly 1.25 inches.

blocks.title: Slotted waveguide array
items: The typical, most common shipboard antenna: waveguide with precisely spaced slots, each radiating a small share.
No separate feed horn. It has largely replaced the truncated parabolic reflector.
End-fed: shows frequency scan, or beam squint: change frequency and the beam swings slightly.
Transmitted lobe: several degrees offset from a line perpendicular to the antenna. Slots sit slightly off ½ guide wavelength to keep VSWR low.

blocks.title: Feed lines
items: ZO, characteristic impedance, is set by how the line is built, not its length. Cut a 72 Ω line at its center: each half is still 72 Ω.
Standing waves: a mismatched load reflects part of the wave, so some energy is not absorbed by the load.
VSWR, voltage standing wave ratio: highest voltage ÷ lowest; 1 to 1 is a perfect match. Measured with a dual directional coupler, power meter and network analyzer.
Long lines not properly shielded and terminated: communications receiver interference might result.

blocks.title: Waveguide
items: A hollow metal pipe of brass, aluminum or copper. Theory: movement of an electromagnetic field; skin effect and ¼ wave stubs.
Why not coax: at microwave frequencies it loses power in its small center conductor and its dielectric. Waveguide has considerably less loss.
Resistive losses are very small because the inner surface is large.
The price: it costs more and is harder to install, but has lower transmission losses.
Stripline: center conductor between parallel ground planes. Microstrip has only 1.

blocks.title: Antenna to display
items: Sweep and antenna are frequently kept in step by synchro systems. Angle is carried on the stator lines.
Resolvers are most common in modern radars: their outputs convert easily to digital bearing data.

blocks.title: Exam traps
items: Coupling capacitance isn't used to get RF in or out.
A narrow vertical beam, high output or high duty cycle doesn't help bearing resolution.
Synchro transmitter: choose 2 rotor, though a standard rotor is 1 winding.
How is direction sent? Any of the above.
